claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds: Ukraine says Starlink access has improved but it is still facing speed limits which are disrupting its battlefield "missions".
- Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania: Buildings were set alight on the second day of demonstrations from thousands of students who want better university conditions and job prospects.
- Retired US generals call on Pentagon to cancel 'barbaric' execution livestream: Livestreaming the execution of Nidal Hasan "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," 72 former officers said in a letter.
- White House defends new press secretary amid questions about her legal credentials: Katie Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.
- 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns: Thick orange smog descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya as wildfires continue raging nearby.
- Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird: Art of Play says its staff have been threatened after the singer complained online about how she was treated.
- Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support: The Irish writer is best known for novels such as Normal People, Intermezzo and Conversations With Friends.
- Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut: It comes as some investors have become concerned about the amount of money being spent on AI infrastructure.
- Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022: The cuts equate to around 6% of the streaming giant's total workforce worldwide.
- Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state: All of the spots are in South Australia, reportedly because the state government paid for incognito inspectors to visit.
- Hundreds of thousands of workers on strike across Republic of Ireland: It comes amidst an an ongoing pay dispute between public sector workers and the Irish government.
- US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices: The pace of price rises increased to 3.7% in the year to September, driving by higher motor fuel costs.
